chemistry.q: An acid reacts with a carbonate (like baking soda). What forms?
options: A salt, water and carbon dioxide
chemistry.why: Acid + carbonate → salt + water + carbon dioxide. The fizzing is CO₂ escaping.

chemistry.q: What is the pH of pure water?
An iron nail in copper(II) sulfate gets coated in copper. Why?
options: Iron is more reactive than copper
Copper is more reactive than iron
chemistry.why: A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its salt solution.

chemistry.q: Why does a higher temperature make a reaction faster?
options: Particles move faster, so more collisions have enough energy
chemistry.why: Faster particles collide more often and more of the collisions reach the activation energy.

chemistry.q: What is the balanced equation for making water?
chemistry.why: 4 hydrogen atoms and 2 oxygen atoms on each side.

biology.why: Random movement spreads particles from where there are many to where there are few.

biology.q: Why does the lion population peak after the antelope population?
options: Lions need time to feed and raise young after food increases
Lions and antelope breed at exactly the same time
biology.why: More prey means more food, but new predators take time to be born and grow.

biology.q: What happens to diffusion when temperature rises?
biology.why: Particles have more kinetic energy and move faster at higher temperatures.

biology.q: Which chamber of the heart pumps blood to the whole body?
biology.why: The left ventricle has the thickest wall and pumps blood into the aorta.

biology.q: Which part do plant cells have but animal cells do not?
biology.why: Chloroplasts carry out photosynthesis; only plant cells have them.

math.q: Compared with y = x², the graph of y = (x − 3)² is…
math.why: Replacing x with (x − h) shifts the graph h units to the right.
At 90° the point on the unit circle is at the top, height 1.

math.q: Which total is most likely when rolling two dice?
math.why: 7 can be made in 6 of the 36 possible ways, more than any other total.

physics.q: Two bulbs are in series. How does the current through them compare?
options: It is the same in both
It is bigger in the first bulb
physics.why: A series circuit has only one path, so the same current flows everywhere.

physics.q: A 6 V battery is connected to a 3 Ω resistor. What is the current?
You add another bulb in parallel. What happens to the total resistance?
physics.why: Each new parallel path gives current another way through, so total resistance decreases.

physics.q: A ball is thrown on flat ground. Which launch angle gives the longest range (no air resistance)?
physics.why: Range depends on sin(2θ), which is biggest when 2θ = 90°, so θ = 45°.
